next_state_election.name: General Election
next_state_election.source_name: Washington Secretary of State — 2026 Dates and Deadlines

glance_notes.source_name: Washington Secretary of State — 2026 Dates and Deadlines
glance_notes.text: Same-Day In-Person Registration: Washington allows eligible residents to register or update their voter registration in person through 8:00 p.m. on Election Day. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, online and mail registrations and updates must be received by October 26.

glance_notes.source_name: Washington Secretary of State — Elections Calendar
glance_notes.text: Statewide Vote-by-Mail: Washington conducts elections by mail. Registered voters are automatically sent ballots, and no absentee excuse or separate ballot request is normally required. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, the 18-day voting period begins October 16.

glance_notes.source_name: Washington Secretary of State — 2026 Dates and Deadlines
glance_notes.text: Ballot Drop Boxes Close at 8:00 p.m.: For the November 3, 2026 General Election, completed ballots may be deposited in an official ballot drop box through 8:00 p.m. on Election Day. Voters returning ballots by mail should allow enough time for the ballot to receive a valid Election Day or earlier postmark.

register.label: Register to Vote
register.content: Eligible Washington residents may register online through VoteWA, by mail or in person. To register, a person must be a U.S. citizen, have lived at a Washington residential address for at least 30 days immediately before Election Day, be at least 18 years old when voting, not be disqualified from voting by a court order and not be serving a sentence of total confinement under the jurisdiction of the Department of Corrections for a Washington felony conviction or currently incarcerated for a federal or out-of-state felony conviction. Washington also operates the Future Voter program, which allows eligible 16- and 17-year-olds to preregister. Eligible residents may register in person through 8:00 p.m. on Election Day.
register.glance_value: Online, mail or in person; same-day registration available
register.source_name: Washington Secretary of State — Register to Vote
register.internal_note: Washington's registration deadline structure is unusually voter-friendly. RCW 29A.08.140 allows online/mail registration through eight days before Election Day and in-person registration through 8:00 p.m. Election Day. Washington's felony voting-rights law changed substantially in 2022: voting rights are automatically restored when a person is no longer serving a sentence of total confinement under Department of Corrections authority. Do not use older language requiring completion of community custody, probation or all sentence conditions.

check_registration.label: Check Voter Registration
check_registration.content: Use VoteWA to check voter registration, update a residential or mailing address, view voter-specific election information, locate ballot drop boxes and voting centers, review voting history and track a ballot. Voters should confirm that their mailing address is current before ballots are mailed.
check_registration.internal_note: VoteWA is Washington's official voter portal. Because Washington automatically mails ballots, both residential and mailing-address accuracy matter. A voter may maintain a mailing address different from the residential voting address.

deadlines.label: Registration Deadlines
deadlines.content: For the November 3, 2026 General Election, new voter registrations and voter-registration updates submitted online or by mail must be received by Monday, October 26. Eligible voters who miss that deadline may register or update their registration in person at a county elections office, voting center or other authorized location through 8:00 p.m. on Election Day.
deadlines.source_name: Washington Secretary of State — 2026 Dates and Deadlines
deadlines.internal_note: The official 2026 calendar explicitly lists October 26 as the deadline to receive new registrations and voter updates online and by mail and November 3 as the in-person deadline. RCW 29A.08.140 confirms the eight-day and Election Day rules. Online submissions are due by midnight on the eight-day deadline; physical applications must be received by election officials by close of business.

polling_place.label: Find a Voting Center or Ballot Drop Box
polling_place.content: Washington is a vote-by-mail state and does not rely on traditional precinct polling places for most voters. Each county provides voting centers where voters can register, obtain replacement ballots, receive assistance and use accessible voting equipment. Counties also provide official ballot drop boxes. Use VoteWA or your county elections office to find current voting-center and drop-box locations and hours.
polling_place.glance_value: Find voting centers and drop boxes through VoteWA
polling_place.internal_note: Do not describe Washington as operating conventional Election Day precinct polling places. Elections are conducted primarily by mail, supplemented by county voting centers and ballot drop boxes. Location-specific information should be retrieved through VoteWA or county election offices near Election Day.

election_day.label: Election Day Voting
election_day.content: Washington's General Election is Tuesday, November 3, 2026. Because Washington conducts elections by mail, most voters return the ballot mailed to them rather than voting at a traditional polling place. Official ballot drop boxes close at 8:00 p.m. on Election Day. Voting centers remain available for in-person voter services, including registration, replacement ballots, accessible voting and ballot assistance. Eligible residents may register or update their registration in person through 8:00 p.m. Election Day.
election_day.glance_value: Drop boxes and in-person registration close at 8:00 p.m.
election_day.source_name: Washington Secretary of State — 2026 Dates and Deadlines
election_day.internal_note: Washington should not receive a conventional 'polls open X to Y' description. The key Election Day cutoff is 8:00 p.m. for official ballot drop boxes and in-person registration. Voting centers provide services through Election Day. County-specific opening hours should be verified locally.

polling_hours.label: Voting Center & Drop Box Hours
polling_hours.content: Washington does not have traditional statewide polling-place hours because elections are conducted by mail. Voting-center schedules vary by county. Accessible Voting Units are available at voting centers beginning with the 18-day voting period and remain available through 8:00 p.m. on Election Day. Official ballot drop boxes close at 8:00 p.m. on Election Day.
polling_hours.glance_value: Election Day cutoff: 8:00 p.m.; voting-center schedules vary
polling_hours.source_name: Washington Secretary of State — Voters with Disabilities
polling_hours.internal_note: Avoid fabricating statewide opening hours. Washington's official accessibility guidance confirms voting-center AVUs from 18 days before Election Day until 8:00 p.m. Election Day. County voting-center schedules vary. The official 2026 deadlines page separately confirms the 8:00 p.m. ballot-drop-box deadline.

early_voting.label: 18-Day Voting Period / In-Person Voting
early_voting.content: Washington's November 3, 2026 General Election voting period begins Friday, October 16 and continues through Election Day. Ballots are mailed to registered voters as the voting period begins. Counties also provide voting centers during the voting period for services that include accessible voting, replacement ballots, registration assistance and in-person voting options. Voting-center locations and schedules vary by county.
early_voting.source_name: Washington Secretary of State — 2026 Dates and Deadlines
early_voting.internal_note: The official 2026 calendar explicitly identifies October 16 as the start of the 18-day General Election voting period and states that ballots are mailed and Accessible Voting Units become available. Washington's system is better described as an 18-day vote-by-mail voting period rather than conventional early voting.

absentee_mail.label: Vote by Mail
absentee_mail.content: Washington conducts elections by mail. Registered voters are automatically mailed a ballot, so most voters do not need to request an absentee ballot or provide an excuse. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, the 18-day voting period begins October 16. Completed ballots may be returned through an official ballot drop box by 8:00 p.m. on Election Day or returned by mail. Washington ballot-return envelopes include prepaid postage. A mailed ballot must receive a valid postmark no later than Election Day to qualify under the ordinary return rule, so voters mailing ballots close to Election Day should confirm collection and postmark timing or use an official drop box.
absentee_mail.glance_value: Ballots automatically mailed; drop boxes close 8:00 p.m. Election Day
absentee_mail.source_name: Washington Secretary of State — Voting by Mail FAQs
absentee_mail.internal_note: Washington is a universal vote-by-mail state. Ballots returned by mail require an Election Day-or-earlier postmark under RCW 29A.40.091. The Secretary of State cautions voters about postal collection times because depositing a ballot in a mailbox on Election Day does not necessarily guarantee an Election Day postmark. Drop boxes provide a clear 8:00 p.m. Election Day cutoff. Return postage is prepaid.

voter_id.label: Voter ID Requirements
voter_id.content: Washington's ordinary vote-by-mail process verifies voters primarily through the signature on the ballot-return declaration rather than requiring voters to submit photo identification with a mailed ballot. A voter using an in-person voting center may be asked for identification depending on the service being requested. Voters who register in person close to or on Election Day should be prepared to provide the identifying information required for voter registration. Election officials compare the signature on a returned ballot declaration with signatures in the voter's registration record and contact the voter when a signature issue must be resolved.
voter_id.glance_value: Mail ballots use signature verification; no general photo-ID requirement
voter_id.source_name: Washington Secretary of State — Voting by Mail FAQs
voter_id.internal_note: Washington should not be labeled a conventional voter-photo-ID state. Ballot authentication is based primarily on signature verification. Do not imply that voters must include a copy of ID with ordinary mailed ballots. Specific identification or identity-verification rules can apply during registration, replacement-ballot requests or other in-person election services.

accessible_voting.label: Accessible Voting
accessible_voting.content: Washington voters with disabilities may request reasonable accommodations and voting assistance. Every county has one or more accessible voting centers, and Accessible Voting Units allow voters with disabilities to mark ballots privately and independently. Accessible Voting Units are available beginning 18 days before Election Day and through 8:00 p.m. on Election Day. Voters who cannot complete a ballot because of a disability may choose someone they trust to assist them or may ask two election workers for assistance. Accessible versions of the state voters' pamphlet are also available.
accessible_voting.glance_value: Accessible Voting Units available October 16 through Election Day
accessible_voting.source_name: Washington Secretary of State — Voters with Disabilities
accessible_voting.internal_note: The Secretary of State confirms that every county has accessible voting centers and that AVUs are available starting 18 days before Election Day through 8:00 p.m. Election Day. Voting centers must meet ADA requirements. A voter may select a trusted assistant or request assistance from two election workers.

military_overseas.label: Military & Overseas Voting
military_overseas.content: Washington provides special voting procedures for eligible military voters, military spouses and dependents, and U.S. citizens living overseas. Military and overseas voters are exempt from the regular voter registration deadline and may register and request a ballot through Election Day. Registration is available through VoteWA when the voter has qualifying identifying information, by paper form or through federal voting-assistance forms. Paper registration forms may be returned to the county elections office by mail, email or fax. Ballots may be delivered by mail, email or fax. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, service and overseas ballots are scheduled to be mailed beginning September 19.
military_overseas.glance_value: Registration through Election Day; ballots begin September 19
military_overseas.source_name: Washington Secretary of State — Military and Overseas Voters
military_overseas.internal_note: Washington's current UOCAVA page expressly states that military and overseas voters are exempt from regular registration deadlines and that Election Day is the final day to register and request a ballot. Ballots can be received by mail, email or fax. The official 2026 calendar identifies September 19 as the service and overseas ballot-mailing date. Do not assume that electronic ballot delivery automatically means all voters may return a voted ballot electronically; follow the current Secretary of State return instructions for the voter's category and method.

student_voting.label: College / Student Voting
student_voting.content: College students may register in Washington if they meet the state's voter eligibility and residency requirements. A voter may be registered at only one residential address. A student temporarily away at college may keep a Washington voting residence and use a different mailing address so the ballot is delivered where the student is living. Students who move their Washington voting residence should update their voter registration. Washington also allows eligible 16- and 17-year-olds to preregister through the Future Voter program, and a 17-year-old who will turn 18 by the November General Election may vote in the August Primary.
student_voting.glance_value: College mailing address may differ; Future Voter preregistration at 16
student_voting.source_name: Washington Secretary of State — Future Voter Program
student_voting.internal_note: The Future Voter program is an important Washington distinction. Eligible 16- and 17-year-olds may preregister and are automatically registered when eligible. A 17-year-old who will be 18 by the November General Election may vote in the preceding August Primary. The official residency page confirms that a voter may use a different mailing address while temporarily away from the registered residence, including while attending college.

sample_ballot.label: Official Ballot & Voters' Pamphlet
sample_ballot.content: Washington voters can use VoteWA to view voter-specific election information and track their mailed ballot. The Secretary of State publishes an official statewide voters' pamphlet for applicable federal and state contests and measures, while counties provide information for local contests and measures. Because ballot contents vary by residential address and political district, voters should use VoteWA and the official voters' pamphlet for the November 3, 2026 General Election when final materials are available.
sample_ballot.glance_value: Use VoteWA and the official voters' pamphlet
sample_ballot.internal_note: Washington provides statewide and local voters' pamphlet information, but a single ballot does not apply to every voter. Final November 2026 ballot contents should be reverified once voter-specific General Election materials are published.

contact.label: Contact the State Election Authority
contact.content: Washington Secretary of State, Elections Division. Mailing address: PO Box 40229, Olympia, WA 98504-0229. Physical location: 416 Sid Snyder Avenue SW, Olympia, WA 98501. Phone: 360-902-4180. Toll-free voter hotline: 800-448-4881. Email: elections@sos.wa.gov. For voter-specific registration, ballot, signature, voting-center or ballot-drop-box questions, contact the appropriate county elections office.
contact.source_name: Washington Secretary of State — Elections Contact Us
contact.internal_note: The current Elections Division contact page verifies 360-902-4180, 800-448-4881, PO Box 40229, Olympia, WA 98504-0229 and 416 Sid Snyder Ave SW, Olympia, WA 98501. The Elections Division email is [elections@sos.wa.gov](mailto:elections@sos.wa.gov). It is intentionally stored as plain text with no Markdown or mailto syntax.

official_resources.label: Official State & Local Resources
official_resources.content: Use the Washington Secretary of State Elections Division, VoteWA and your county elections office for official election information. These resources provide voter registration, voter-record updates, ballot tracking, voting-center and ballot-drop-box locations, election dates, accessible voting information, military and overseas voting guidance, voters' pamphlets and voter-specific election information. Washington counties administer ballot mailing and processing, voting centers, ballot drop boxes and local election operations.
official_resources.glance_value: Secretary of State, VoteWA & county elections offices
